stem: In a patient with a fourth nerve palsy, what clinical presentation is most common?

options.text: A longstanding head tilt to the opposite side of the affected eye.
An inability to abduct the eye (move it outward).
A large pupil and ptosis (droopy eyelid).
The eye retracting into the socket upon looking inward.

explanation: Patients with a fourth nerve palsy often tilt their head to compensate for the vertical misalignment caused by a weak superior oblique muscle.
rationale: Think about the compensatory posture a child might adopt to deal with vertical double vision.

optionExplanations.A: Patients with a fourth nerve palsy often tilt their head to compensate for the vertical misalignment caused by a weak superior oblique muscle.
optionExplanations.B: Inability to abduct is characteristic of a sixth nerve palsy, which affects the lateral rectus.
optionExplanations.C: These are classic signs of a third nerve palsy, not a fourth nerve palsy.
optionExplanations.D: Eye retraction and narrowing of the palpebral fissure are features of Dwayne syndrome.
